next-actions.action: Merge the handoff-protocol branch into the working branch. Re-run the gate. Then close task 5.2 against a receipt naming its three requirements and their audits.

Close the payer-binding gap from AUDIT-OPUS-5-1A. The lender capability assertion proves the lender knows the secret; it does not make the lender the funder, and nothing debits the borrower. Both value legs draw from the submitting transaction's offer with no payer bound. Amounts are constrained, party attribution is not. This is the substantive remainder of 5.1a.
Task 5.3: run test:ledger, test:compiled, test:finalized-state and test:preview, and obtain an exact-source audit. The suites already pass; the audit leg is what is missing.
Task 5.4 onward: Docker lifecycle, then Preview. Preview is a testnet and its tokens are worthless; do not treat a funded transaction there as a high-risk action.

blocked-on-owner.item: Obligation 127 freezes all K retry until there is a grounded change or proposal, fresh independent audits, and root admission. The proposal exists at deliverables/language-to-ledger-2026-09-12/k-proposal/. The audits and admission do not.

The plugin gate blocks dependent dispatch on four evidence gaps: two stale input hashes on openspec/sprints/sp01-financial-contract-and-execution-admission.md, a missing .moriarty-dev/runtime/current-accounting.json, and no live state for resource sp01-loan-swap-grok-01. None is a funding gap. Re-sealing the stale binding is a decision about what counts as the verified basis.

hard-constraints.constraint: plugins/moriarty-dev/hooks/hooks.json embeds a SHA-256 digest over every .py file under scripts/moriarty_dev, currently 0b40d8c3e184f246... appearing four times. Editing any of those .py files without re-pinning all four occurrences in the same change makes every hook fail closed and stops tool interception across the environment. Recompute as: sha256 of each file keyed by path relative to that directory, JSON with sorted keys and separators (",",":"), then sha256 of that JSON. Also place the updated tree at ~/.local/share/moriarty-dev/runtimes/<digest>/.

Never create, reset or zero any accounting, budget, charge, reservation or resource record. Consumed charges and recorded failures are evidence. Do not write .moriarty-dev/runtime/current-accounting.json from zero.

Several suites deliberately refuse to rebuild and verify pinned hashes instead. Never regenerate a retained build artifact. custody/generate.mjs is itself pinned in build-proven.mjs REQUIRED_SOURCES; editing it breaks three suites. An earlier round learned this and moved its emitter to generate-lifecycle.mjs.
No roadmap checkbox may be ticked without a corresponding evidence receipt.

Never write Co-Authored-By, Claude-Session, or any model or session attribution into a commit, tag or pull request. Run: git log --all --grep='Co-Authored-By' --grep='Claude-Session' --grep='Claude Code' before any push and refuse if it matches. Moriarty is clean. The separate ~/foreman repo has 38 such commits already on its remote, which is a known and separate problem.

Scan before committing and pushing, not after. A prior session pushed 804 files to this public repo first. Eleven scraped pages carrying key material were removed afterwards; they remain in earlier history.

lessons-that-cost-time.lesson: Re-run every count yourself. Lane reports were wrong or incomplete in most rounds. Audits caught a test asserting broken behaviour as correct, a success gate fed invented zeros, and a boot-mismatch denial with no code path.

Dispatch through queue admission bound to an Endstop contract, wrapped in lane-run.sh --round. Six of six directly dispatched agent lanes stranded by backgrounding their vendor and stopping. Zero of five queue-admitted rounds did.
lane-run.sh --round takes the worktree PATH, not its slug, and prints a generic usage line when given a slug.
Use a gate that actually runs tests. tools/ci-local.sh --quick has no typecheck and no unit-test gate and passes while verifying nothing.
Create lane worktrees from a base containing the work they depend on. Four lanes inherited two test failures from an uncommitted fix.

The retained macro05 failure is the LLVM interpreter at exit 113. The kore-expand-macros fault at exit 139 belongs to the earlier parse04 attempt, and only that one is covered by documented upstream exclusion CLM-0524.
